§1 · Introduction

The big idea

Recursive self-improvement need not start with a model rewriting its weights. It can start in the harness.

I. J. Good described an “ultraintelligent machine” that designs better machines. Yudkowsky framed recursive self-improvement as a loop in which an AI uses its current intelligence to improve the machinery that produces it. The post widens the loop: a model can also improve its training pipeline or its deployment system.

That deployment system is the harness: the code around a base model that decides how it plans, calls tools, manages context, stores artifacts and evaluates results. The post argues the harness matters about as much as raw model intelligence, and that the near-term path to self-improvement runs through it.

Our reading frame

One loop for every method

Every method on this site is drawn as the same seven-box loop, with the same symbols.

A self-improving harness keeps an archive 𝒜 of past versions. It selects a parent, a proposer writes a candidate H′, the base model runs the candidate on tasks, an evaluator scores it, and an accept rule decides what enters the archive. Methods differ only in how they fill these boxes.

§2.1–2.3

Harness design patterns

Three patterns recur: a goal-oriented loop, files as memory, and explicit parallel work.

Modern harnesses go beyond “LLM plus memory plus tools”. They add workflow design, evaluation, permission controls and persistent state. The post asks for designs that stay simple and generic, like an operating system that hides complex logic behind a small interface.

§2.5

Harness layer vs core intelligence

The post predicts three stages before models rewrite their own weights.

Step-through

Where improvement lives, stage by stage

Illustrative

Today: people hand-write prompt tricks and harness rules around a fixed model.

Stage 1: harness engineering becomes a meta-methodology. It improves the machinery that produces answers, with fewer heuristic rules and more general mechanisms.

Stage 2: mature harnesses run auto-research and self-improvement loops that help produce smarter models, which in turn need less harness engineering.

Stage 3: harness gains may be internalized into the model, as instruction tuning absorbed prompt tricks. The interface to tools and context remains.

Self-check

Check yourself

Six questions on the whole post.

1.Why does the post expect self-improvement to start in the harness rather than in the weights?

Code is a universal language for systems. Once the harness is code, coding agents can search it like engineers do, while weight updates stay harder to control.

2.ACE merges delta bullets instead of rewriting the prompt. Which failure does that prevent?

Whole rewrites tend to compress accumulated knowledge into a short summary. Itemized, deterministic merges keep each bullet.

3.What did STOP find when it used weaker base models?

GPT-4 improved its improver; GPT-3.5 and Mixtral got worse. A recursive structure alone is not enough: the base model must be capable enough.

4.In Self-Harness, when is a proposed edit accepted?

Validation runs regression tests on both splits. Only edits that fix weaknesses without new failures are merged; rejected edits are logged.

5.DGM samples parents in proportion to score times 1/(1 + number of children). Why the second factor?

Favoring members with few children spreads search across the open-ended archive and works against diversity collapse.

6.Where does the post want evaluators and permission controls to sit?

A loop optimizes whatever signal it gets. If it can edit the verifier, it can hack the reward. AHE makes those files read-only.

  1. A harness decides how a model plans, acts, remembers and checks. The post argues it matters as much as raw capability.
  2. Optimization targets climbed from prompts to context, workflows, harness code and the optimizer code itself.
  3. Every method is one loop: archive, select, propose, execute, evaluate, accept. They differ in how each box is filled.
  4. Loops work when evaluation is fast and objective. Weak evaluators, reward hacking and diversity collapse remain open.

    The whole chain to this method

      Check yourself

      1.What is the main change from ADAS to AFlow?

      ADAS shows the meta-agent a flat archive. AFlow stores workflows in a tree and picks the node to expand by mixing score and exploration.

      2.What makes Hyperagents different from DGM?

      DGM’s self-modification procedure is fixed. Hyperagents puts the task agent and the meta agent in one editable program.

      3.Which pair moves from frozen LLMs to training the proposer’s weights?

      ThetaEvolve keeps AlphaEvolve’s program database but trains one small model with RL on its own evolution rollouts.

      Our synthesis

      A starting point drawn from the post’s discussion, not a rule. Each answer opens the method on Evolution.

      Check yourself

      1.Which two methods have the same model propose edits to its own harness, with no stronger meta-agent?

      Self-Harness runs the proposer as the same fixed model. STOP’s improver queries the same LM to rewrite itself. Meta-Harness and ADAS use a separate, stronger proposer.

      2.Meta-Harness and GEPA both keep a Pareto set. What does each use it for?

      Meta-Harness returns the accuracy–cost frontier as its result. GEPA samples parents from per-instance winners on its Pareto set.

      NoteThe post uses each paper’s own symbols, which clash (α is a temperature in AFlow and a threshold in ShinkaEvolve). This site adds one shared set for the loop diagrams and keeps paper symbols in formula cards.
      How symbols are writtenEquations are typeset with MathJax. Symbols in text, tables and diagrams follow the same rules: italic variables, upright words and script letters, real subscripts. Code names use monospace.
